domain_entities.name: LeaveRequest
domain_entities.purpose: Represents an employee's application for leave. Tracks the full lifecycle from draft through approval/rejection to cancellation, carrying the dates, type, and reason for the absence.
lifecycle_states: DRAFT: Employee has created but not yet submitted the request. Editable by the employee.
SUBMITTED: Employee has submitted for manager review. Awaiting approval or rejection.
APPROVED: Manager has approved the request. Balance has been deducted. The leave is confirmed.
REJECTED: Manager has rejected the request. Terminal state — no balance impact.
CANCELLED: Request was withdrawn. If cancelled from APPROVED, balance is restored. If cancelled from DRAFT or SUBMITTED, no balance impact. Terminal state.
State transitions:
DRAFT → SUBMITTED: Employee submits the request (submit)
DRAFT → CANCELLED: Employee discards the draft (cancel)
SUBMITTED → APPROVED: Manager approves the request (approve)
SUBMITTED → REJECTED: Manager rejects the request (reject)
SUBMITTED → CANCELLED: Employee withdraws the submitted request (withdraw)
APPROVED → CANCELLED: Employee cancels an approved leave (cancelApproved) — triggers balance restoration

domain_entities.name: LeavePolicy
domain_entities.purpose: Defines the rules and entitlements for a specific leave type. Governs how many days an employee is entitled to, whether manager approval is required, minimum notice periods, and accrual behaviour.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: Policy is in effect and governs leave requests.
INACTIVE: Policy has been disabled; no new requests can reference it. Existing approved leave under this policy is unaffected.

domain_entities.name: LeaveBalance
domain_entities.purpose: Tracks an employee's leave entitlement, usage, and remaining balance for a specific leave policy within a fiscal year. Deducted on approval, restored on cancellation of approved leave.
lifecycle_states: ACTIVE: Balance is in effect for the current fiscal year. Leave deductions and restorations apply.
EXHAUSTED: remainingDays has reached 0. No further leave of this type can be taken until the next fiscal year or accrual replenishes it.
CLOSED: Fiscal year has ended. Balance is archived and a new balance record is created for the next year.

domain_entities.name: LeaveNotification
domain_entities.purpose: Domain event notification triggered by leave lifecycle transitions. Sent to employees (status updates on their requests) and managers (new requests to approve). Also triggered when balance crosses thresholds.
lifecycle_states: PENDING: Notification created but not yet delivered.
SENT: Notification has been delivered to the recipient.
READ: Recipient has acknowledged/read the notification.
ARCHIVED: Notification is no longer shown in the active inbox.

domain_entities.name: LeaveType
domain_entities.purpose: Enumeration of leave categories. Each LeavePolicy is associated with exactly one LeaveType. The type determines the policy's behaviour (e.g. sick leave may not require advance notice, annual leave may accrue).

business_rules: startDate must be on or before endDate. A LeaveRequest with startDate > endDate is invalid at submission time. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

Leave days are counted as calendar days inclusive of both startDate and endDate: daysRequested = (endDate - startDate) + 1. This count is used uniformly for balance sufficiency checks and balance deductions. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

On transition from SUBMITTED to APPROVED: the employee's LeaveBalance for the matching policy and current fiscal year must have remainingDays >= daysRequested. If insufficient, the approval must be rejected with a balance-insufficient error. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

On APPROVED → CANCELLED: the LeaveBalance usedDays is decremented by daysRequested and remainingDays is incremented by the same amount. The balance status may transition from EXHAUSTED back to ACTIVE. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

If the LeavePolicy referenced by leaveTypeId has minimumNoticeDays set, then at submission time: (startDate - today) must be >= minimumNoticeDays. If the policy has requiresManagerApproval = false, the request auto-transitions to APPROVED on submission (no manager action needed). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

An employee must not have two overlapping APPROVED LeaveRequests. Overlap is defined as: requestA.startDate <= requestB.endDate AND requestB.startDate <= requestA.endDate. This check runs on the SUBMITTED → APPROVED transition. If an overlap exists, approval is rejected. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

Only the employee who owns the request (employeeId) may submit (DRAFT → SUBMITTED), withdraw (SUBMITTED → CANCELLED), or cancel an approved request (APPROVED → CANCELLED). Only a manager (the employee's managerId or an HR admin) may approve or reject (SUBMITTED → APPROVED / REJECTED). [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]

An employee must have employmentStatus = 'ACTIVE' at the time of submission (DRAFT → SUBMITTED). Terminated or inactive employees cannot submit leave requests. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, Employee appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest can only reference a LeavePolicy whose isActive = true at the time of submission. Referencing an inactive policy is rejected. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeavePolicy appears, not only here]

On SUBMITTED → APPROVED: the LeaveBalance usedDays is incremented by daysRequested and remainingDays is decremented by daysRequested. If remainingDays reaches 0, the balance status transitions to EXHAUSTED. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest, LeaveBalance appears, not only here]

A LeaveRequest is only editable (startDate, endDate, reason, leaveTypeId) while in DRAFT state. Once SUBMITTED, the request is immutable except for status transitions. [BINDING RULE — apply this wherever LeaveRequest appears, not only here]
domain_notes:
## Lifecycle states introduced

- **LeaveRequest**: DRAFT, SUBMITTED, APPROVED, REJECTED, CANCELLED — with six named transitions: submit, cancel (from DRAFT), approve, reject, withdraw (from SUBMITTED), cancelApproved (from APPROVED).
- **LeavePolicy**: ACTIVE, INACTIVE — simple enable/disable toggle.
- **LeaveBalance**: ACTIVE, EXHAUSTED, CLOSED — tracks fiscal-year lifecycle with automatic status changes on deduction and year-end.
- **LeaveNotification**: PENDING, SENT, READ, ARCHIVED — standard notification delivery lifecycle.

## Key business rules (broad scope)

- **BR-calendar-days**: daysRequested = (endDate - startDate) + 1, applied uniformly to sufficiency checks and balance mutations.
- **BR-balance-sufficiency**: Approval blocked if remainingDays < daysRequested.
- **BR-balance-deduction**: APPROVED increments usedDays, decrements remainingDays; CANCELLED (from APPROVED) reverses this.
- **BR-no-overlap**: No two APPROVED requests for the same employee may overlap in date ranges.
- **BR-policy-gate**: Submission requires active policy; minimumNoticeDays enforced; requiresManagerApproval=false triggers auto-approval.
- **BR-actor-rbac**: Employee-only actions (submit, withdraw, cancelApproved) vs manager-only actions (approve, reject).
- **BR-active-employee**: Only ACTIVE employees may submit.
- **BR-draft-immutability**: Only DRAFT requests are editable; SUBMITTED+ are immutable except for status transitions.

## Open questions for chief architect

- Fiscal year boundary definition (calendar vs configurable).
- Leave day counting granularity (calendar days vs business days vs business-days-minus-holidays).
- Minimum leave granularity (full days vs half days vs hours).

open_questions.question: How is the fiscal year boundary defined — calendar year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) or a configurable start month/day? This determines when LeaveBalance transitions from ACTIVE/EXHAUSTED to CLOSED and when new balance records are created.
open_questions.impact: Affects LeaveBalance lifecycle, balance rollover logic, and the accrual scheduler. If configurable, the policy module needs a fiscalYearStart field.
candidate_options: Configurable per policy or per organisation (e.g. April 6 – April 5 for UK tax year)
Configurable globally via a system setting

open_questions.question: Should leave duration count weekends and public holidays as leave days, or only business days? The current rule uses calendar days inclusive, but this may not match all organisational policies.
open_questions.impact: Affects the daysRequested calculation, balance sufficiency checks, and balance deductions. If business-days-only is chosen, a holiday calendar entity is needed.
candidate_options: Calendar days (all days counted, including weekends and holidays)
Business days excluding public holidays (requires a holiday calendar)

open_questions.question: What is the minimum granularity of a leave request — full days, half days, or hours? This affects the daysRequested calculation and balance precision.
open_questions.impact: Affects LeaveRequest validation, LeaveBalance precision (integer vs decimal), and the daysRequested formula. Half-day support requires startDate/endDate to carry time-of-day or an AM/PM flag.
